mcqs.question: When two transverse waves traveling in the same medium intersect, what is the resultant displacement at any point?

options.A: The algebraic sum of the individual displacements of the two waves
options.B: The product of the individual displacements of the two waves
options.C: The average of the individual displacements of the two waves
options.D: The larger of the two individual displacements

mcqs.answer: The algebraic sum of the individual displacements of the two waves
mcqs.explanation: The principle of superposition states that when two or more waves overlap, the resultant displacement at any point is the vector (algebraic) sum of the displacements due to each wave. Hence option A is correct. Options B, C and D describe operations that are not part of the superposition principle.

mcqs.question: Two identical speakers emit sound waves of the same frequency and amplitude. They are positioned so that the waves arrive in phase at point P. What is the amplitude of the resultant wave at P compared to the amplitude of the wave from a single speaker?

options.A: Twice the amplitude of a single speaker
options.B: The same amplitude as a single speaker
options.D: Half the amplitude of a single speaker

mcqs.answer: Twice the amplitude of a single speaker
mcqs.explanation: When two waves of equal amplitude are in phase, their displacements add constructively, giving a resultant amplitude equal to the sum of the individual amplitudes. Therefore the amplitude becomes 2A, i.e., twice that of one speaker. Options B, C and D contradict the constructive addition rule.

mcqs.question: Which of the following statements about destructive interference is incorrect?

options.A: It occurs when two waves of equal amplitude are 180° out of phase.
options.B: It always results in zero net displacement regardless of the amplitudes of the interfering waves.
options.C: It can reduce the resultant amplitude compared to the individual amplitudes.
options.D: It follows from the principle of superposition.

mcqs.answer: It always results in zero net displacement regardless of the amplitudes of the interfering waves.
mcqs.explanation: Destructive interference leads to cancellation only when the interfering waves have equal amplitudes and are exactly 180° out of phase. If the amplitudes differ, the resultant displacement is reduced but not zero. Hence statement B is the misconception. Statements A, C and D correctly describe aspects of destructive interference.

mcqs.question: Two coherent sources emit waves of the same frequency. If the phase difference between them at a certain point is 90°, what type of interference is observed at that point?

options.C: Partial constructive interference, giving a resultant amplitude of √2 times the amplitude of one wave

mcqs.answer: Partial constructive interference, giving a resultant amplitude of √2 times the amplitude of one wave
mcqs.explanation: When the phase difference φ = 90°, the resultant amplitude is 2A·cos(φ/2) = 2A·cos45° = 2A·(√2/2) = √2 A. This is neither fully constructive nor fully destructive, so the interference is partial constructive. Options A and B describe the extreme cases (0° and 180°), while D is incorrect because interference always occurs when waves overlap.

mcqs.question: Which statement correctly distinguishes the principle of superposition from the principle of energy conservation?

options.A: Superposition states that the net displacement of overlapping waves is the algebraic sum of individual displacements, whereas energy conservation deals with the total energy of the system remaining constant.
options.B: Superposition deals with the total energy of interacting waves, while energy conservation deals with the sum of their amplitudes.
options.C: Both principles assert that the resultant amplitude is always equal to the sum of individual amplitudes.
options.D: Superposition is applicable only to mechanical waves, whereas energy conservation applies only to electromagnetic waves.

mcqs.answer: Superposition states that the net displacement of overlapping waves is the algebraic sum of individual displacements, whereas energy conservation deals with the total energy of the system remaining constant.
mcqs.explanation: The principle of superposition concerns how wave displacements combine (addition of amplitudes). Energy conservation is a separate law stating that the total energy of an isolated system does not change. Option A captures this distinction. Options B, C and D mix up the concepts or impose incorrect restrictions.

mcqs.question: Two coherent light beams of equal intensity I₀ interfere constructively. What is the intensity at points of maximum constructive interference?
mcqs.explanation: For coherent beams of equal amplitude, constructive interference doubles the resultant amplitude (A_total = 2A). Since intensity I ∝ amplitude², the intensity becomes (2A)² = 4A², i.e., four times the intensity of a single beam. Therefore the maximum intensity is 4 I₀. Options A, B and D underestimate the intensity increase.

mcqs.question: Destructive interference between two waves of the same frequency occurs when the phase difference between them is:
mcqs.explanation: When two identical waves are exactly out of phase (180° phase difference), their displacements are opposite at every point, leading to cancellation—this is destructive interference. 0° gives constructive interference, 90° gives partial interference, and 360° is equivalent to 0°.

mcqs.question: If two waves of equal amplitude A have a phase difference φ, the resultant amplitude of the superposed wave is:
mcqs.explanation: Using vector addition of two equal-amplitude phasors separated by φ, the magnitude of the resultant is 2A cos(φ⁄2). This formula directly relates phase difference to the resultant amplitude. Options B, C, and D represent incorrect trigonometric relationships.
